info.name: Blog Application REST API
info.description:
REST API for a Blog Management Application with Guest, User, and Admin access.

Base URL: http://localhost:5000

Auth: Bearer JWT from POST /api/auth/login.

## Self-contained

Everything lives in this one file. Do NOT select an environment when you run it. If one is selected it must not define userId, blogId or token, because Postman resolves an environment variable before a collection variable of the same name. The collection pre-request script clears those keys from the active environment for exactly that reason. baseUrl is deliberately left alone, so an environment may still repoint the host.

## Repeatable, and safe for several people at once

Register User mints a fresh runId on every send and derives a unique email from it (qa.user.<runId>@example.com), so the collection can be run any number of times, by any number of people, against one shared database without hitting 409 email already registered.

The run's blogs carry the same runId in title and category, so the public search and filter requests match this run's own rows rather than data somebody else left behind.

Three identities are kept apart in their own variables: userToken (the run's user), user2Token (a second ordinary user, used for the cross-owner 403 checks) and adminToken. Sharing one token variable would let the admin login silently take over the user requests, which then rewrites the admin's own profile and password.

## Needs the seeded admin

Run `npm run seed:admin` before the collection. Login Admin must succeed (200) with `admin@example.com` / `password123` and stores `adminToken` / `adminUserId`. Admin-only requests then run for real; they are not skipped.

## Run order

Run the collection top to bottom. Deactivate User is followed immediately by Reactivate User, otherwise every later request carrying userToken answers 403. Cleanup is last so the public reads still have blogs to find.

// with userId=1 / blogId=1 / empty token would make almost every test 401 or 403.
// unset is a no-op when the key is absent or no environment is selected.
// do not use pm.environment.has — older Postman builds throw, which aborts

item.name: Cleanup
item.description:
Runs last so the folders above still have data to read. Deletes the three blogs this run created, which is what keeps a shared database from filling up when the collection is run over and over.

The user rows stay: the API has no delete-user endpoint, and every run registers fresh emails anyway.

request.description: Negative case, deliberately before the real delete so there is still something to refuse.

exec: pm.test('says the caller is not authorized', () => {
pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('You are not authorized to delete this blog.');

request.description: Negative case, user against user. Ownership is enforced on delete exactly as on update.
Submission path DELETE /api/blogs/delete/:id. Owner or admin.
Tidies up the row created by Create Blog Body Ignores userId.

exec: pm.test('200 OK, the owner may delete their own blog', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description: The same row the 403 above could not touch, now deleted by its actual owner. Tidies up Create Second User's Blog.

exec: pm.test('404 Not Found, the delete really removed the row', () => pm.response.to.have.status(404));

request.description: Confirms the delete rather than trusting the 200 above.
